data.title: Nvidia Faces Explosive SEC Accounting Probe as China Spy Scandal Deepens — What Wall Street Sees Next
data.description:
Just when investors thought Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) had enough problems to deal with, another potentially damaging development has arrived from Washington. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating the AI leader's accounting practices, according to Reuters, adding another headache to the fallout surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang's scandal. With Nvidia already suffering heavy stock market losses, the latest investigation threatens to make its recovery even more challenging.

And the accounting probe isn't the only concern weighing on investor confidence right now. A separate New York Times investigation has uncovered extensive connections between Alice Huang, the woman at the center of Jensen's affair and alleged espionage activities, and China's defense industry. Taken together, these developments raise concerns about Nvidia's financial reporting, corporate oversight, and potential exposure to Chinese military interests.

SEC Investigation Opens Another Front for Nvidia

According to Reuters reporters Chris Prentice and Alexandra Alper, two people briefed on the matter confirmed that federal regulators are examining Nvidia's accounting practices. The disclosure follows an earlier Wall Street Journal article revealing an SEC investigation, although that initial account did not establish its focus.

The latest development introduces another source of uncertainty for investors already dealing with Nvidia's leadership crisis. While the precise accounting issues remain undisclosed, any investigation involving financial reporting could have serious implications for investor confidence, especially following the departure of such an influential CEO.

Still, an SEC investigation does not establish wrongdoing, and regulators have yet to announce any findings against Nvidia.

Alice Huang's Alleged China Connections Raise Further Concerns

Meanwhile, the New York Times has uncovered additional information surrounding Alice Huang's connections to China's military-industrial network. Citing corporate filings and research conducted by an independent organization, the newspaper described extensive relationships involving her relatives, associates, and companies purchasing Nvidia technology.

Several of those connections ultimately lead to Chinese state-owned defense contractors supplying equipment to the People's Liberation Army. However, many relationships are indirect, while their precise nature remains unclear, leaving important uncertainties surrounding any potential national-security implications.

These revelations arrive at an especially sensitive moment for Nvidia, given Washington's existing restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports to China. Although the findings do not establish that Nvidia knowingly supplied technology to Chinese military organizations, they could encourage further scrutiny of its overseas commercial relationships.

What Does Wall Street See Ahead for NVDA Stock?

Despite the growing controversy, Wall Street continues to see considerable upside potential for Nvidia over the coming year. According to TipRanks, the stock currently holds a Moderate Buy consensus rating, reflecting 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and just one Sell issued during the past three months. The average 12-month price target stands at $232.59, suggesting ~82% upside from current levels.

Ultimately, Wall Street's bullish outlook suggests analysts still believe Nvidia's long-term growth prospects outweigh its immediate challenges. Whether that confidence proves justified may depend on what federal investigators uncover in the coming weeks. (See NVDA stock forecast)

data.title: Nasdaq Plunges as AI Selloff Deepens
data.description:
Technology and AI stocks continued to face heavy selling pressure on Friday following Thursday's sharp market decline. Shares of Claude creator Anthropic (ANT) also fell after the company's Nasdaq debut yesterday. Anthropic closed its first trading day at $97.17 per share, up by 17% from its $83 IPO price. The company raised approximately $81.3 billion by selling 980 million shares.

Concerns about high AI valuations and the enormous costs of developing artificial intelligence continued to weigh on the market. At the time of writing, the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) is down by 3.7%, while the S&P 500 (SPY) is down by 1.95%. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones (DIA) fell by 0.45%.

The losses followed a difficult Thursday session in which all three major U.S. stock indexes declined by more than 2%. Stocks had initially risen before reversing course, with the Dow closing below 50,000 for the first time since June. The continued weakness has put all three indexes on track to finish the week with losses.

Oil prices also declined on Friday as expectations of a global supply surplus outweighed concerns about disruptions in the Middle East. According to Reuters, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have added uncertainty to the supply outlook.

However, crude shipments through the waterway have returned to roughly pre-war levels. Brent crude futures fell by 0.75% to $88.77 per barrel, while WTI crude futures declined by 0.47% to $82.05 per barrel.

Intuit Offloads Mailchimp

Separately, Intuit (INTU) shares dropped after the tax software company announced a $3.68 billion sale of Mailchimp to Bending Spoons (BSP). Intuit also lowered its full-year revenue forecast due to weaker expectations for its Credit Karma business. Meanwhile, off-price retailer Ross Stores (ROST) traded lower after its fourth-quarter earnings outlook disappointed Wall Street.

In contrast, clothing retailer Gap (GAP) rose after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter earnings. Health insurer UnitedHealth (UNH) also gained after TD Cowen upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold. Analyst Ryan Langston named UnitedHealth the firm's "2027 Best Idea" and increased his price target to $455 from $402. He also upgraded rival health insurer Humana (HUM) to Buy from Hold.

data.title: JPMorgan Strategist Says Tech Stocks Were Overdue for a Correction. Here's Why
data.description:
The recent technology stock selloff was overdue, according to JPMorgan Asset Management chief global strategist David Kelly. In an interview with CNBC, Kelly explained that tech stocks had risen so much that a pullback was becoming increasingly likely. He pointed to recent problems at chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) and changes in the technology industry as reasons for the weakness. His comments came as the S&P 500 (SPX) fell by roughly 10% from its October record on Friday, while the Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) continued to decline.

One reason for the uncertainty is Nvidia's recent leadership change. The company's longtime CEO, Jensen Huang, resigned last week, which has left investors wondering how the business will perform without him.

However, Nvidia's financial results remain strong. Its third-quarter revenue grew by 103% to $115.8 billion, while data center revenue increased by 110% to $107.6 billion. Despite that growth, the stock has continued to fall.

Kelly believes that the weakness in technology stocks does not necessarily mean that the entire U.S. economy is in trouble. In fact, he sees little evidence that demand is strong enough outside the technology industry to cause inflation to rise sharply. That is one reason why he believes that the Federal Reserve may not need to increase interest rates as much as some expect.

Why Kelly Expects the Federal Reserve to Slow Down

Kelly expects inflation to ease in the coming months, partly because gasoline prices have fallen. He estimates that lower gasoline prices alone could reduce November's annual Consumer Price Index inflation rate by about 0.4 percentage points.

The housing market also supports his view that the economy is slowing. For example, U.S. permits for new single-family homes declined by 8.7% in October. Since builders typically need permits before starting construction, fewer permits suggest that they expect less demand for new homes.

Because of these signs of weakness, Kelly disagrees with Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller's support for a possible 50-basis-point interest rate increase in December.

Kelly expects the Fed to raise rates in December and then stop increasing them for a while. He argues that interest rates are already near levels that should prevent the economy from growing too quickly. Therefore, additional large increases could put unnecessary pressure on economic activity.

Despite the recent stock market losses, Kelly also believes that several factors could help prices recover. Americans continue to invest money through their retirement accounts, which creates regular demand for stocks. Companies also support their share prices by buying back their own shares.

Is SPY ETF a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), which tracks the overall stock market in the U.S. This is based on 414 Buys, 83 Holds, and six Sells assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average SPY price target of $911.58 per share implies 30.2% upside potential. (See SPY Stock Forecast).

data.title: Intel 18A Yields Hit 70%, Intel Stock (NASDAQ:INTC) Drops Over 5%
data.description:
Chip stock Intel (INTC) recently landed a big win by bringing Microsoft (MSFT) into the fold as a customer for its 18A process. But with that new deal comes an exciting corollary; it turns out that Intel has now reached production yields of over 70%, according to a report from Tom's Hardware. Intel stock dropped over 5% in Friday afternoon's trading, and Intel has seen a 65.73% rally in its share price over the past year.

The Yield's The Thing

Landing a major corporate partner was a big advance, but it got even better when we realized that getting that big advance required Intel to be able to produce enough chips this way to make it worthwhile. This means Intel's yield on the 18A process has cleared 70%. Back in March of 2025, when Lip-Bu Tan took over as CEO of Intel, the yields for 18A were what he described as horrible. Now they are up to 70%, which is right in line for a comparatively new technology that is gaining ground.

Tan did not clarify what kind of yield was involved, whether it was parametric yield, functional yield, or a percentage of "sellable silicon". But, it is likely that he was referring to functional die yield, or the portion of dies that can clear basic testing for electrical conductivity and function. This is certainly a good point for Intel to be at right now, though there are still some potential issues of parametric yield and the number of advanced processors that Intel can supply to customers.

Backing the Future

Intel recently announced the winners of its 2026 Intel AI Global Impact Festival, an event designed around bringing together students and other developers to put artificial intelligence to work to address various societal challenges. Several projects stood out in particular, with a range of functions designed to bridge cultural gaps or carry out other functions.

One such project was known as FluentifyAI, which was designed to help Japanese learners of English improve their pronunciation and also get bilingual feedback as well as sets of practice exercises. All of that voice data, meanwhile, was kept strictly private. Another, known as PlagueBot VR, was designed to help with pest management as well as reducing pesticide usage when it comes to tomato farming. This system brought together a RealSense depth camera and OpenVINO Edge AI vision.

data.title: Gold Prices Sink Toward Worst Week Since March as AI Stock Losses Trigger Cash Scramble
data.description:
Spot gold (CM:XAUUSD) fell 3.01% to $3,516.98 per ounce on Friday, hitting its weakest level since September 2025, TipRanks data shows. Bullion has dropped roughly 8% this week and 12.10% over the past month, putting the metal on track for its largest weekly slide since March.

Other precious metals also fell on Friday. Silver (CM:XAGUSD) dropped past $42 per ounce toward a 14% weekly loss, while platinum (CM:XPTUSD) slipped 2.7% to $1,308.

Investors Have Been Selling Gold to Cover Tech Stock Losses

Global equities fell for a seventh straight day on Friday, marking the longest losing streak for the MSCI All Country World Index since September 2023, Bloomberg reported. Large losses in AI and semiconductor shares pushed investors to sell liquid gold holdings to cover tech stock losses.

Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank, wrote on Friday that "bullion has become a source of cash for investors facing mounting losses elsewhere." Real Macro founder Jeff Currie told Kitco that traders typically dump precious metals first to raise dollars during a market cash squeeze.

In addition, XTB analysts noted that gold's 60-day price correlation with global stocks climbed to 0.46 in 2026, up from an average of 0.14 between 2019 and 2024, because many tech investors also hold bullion.

Gold Faces Pressure From Fed Rate Bets and Real Yields

Expectations for higher U.S. borrowing costs added pressure on gold, since bullion pays no interest to holders.

Futures markets priced in a 97% to 99% chance of a quarter-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, CME FedWatch data shows.

Meanwhile, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) held near a 19-month high of 103.8, making dollar-priced gold more expensive for overseas investors as 10-year inflation-adjusted Treasury yields sat near 2.86%.

Friday's U.S. economic reports offered mixed signals for rate watchers. The University of Michigan's final November consumer sentiment index ticked up to 51.5 as year-ahead inflation expectations fell from 4.7% to 3.7%.

At the same time, the Philadelphia Fed's factory prices-paid gauge jumped from 43.2 to 58.2, its highest reading since April.

Gold Has Drawn in Asian Bargain Hunters Near $3,500 Support

Lower bullion prices are starting to test gold miners after industry all-in sustaining costs rose 22% year over year to $1,930 per ounce in the second quarter, World Gold Council figures show.

Physical investors in Asia are treating the pullback as a discount, with Indian gold premiums doubling from $8 to $17 an ounce during wedding season and Chinese premiums reaching $9 to $13, XTB reported.

Long-term institutional holders have also stayed resilient, with global gold ETFs holding a record 4,275 metric tons entering November, World Gold Council data show.

Analysts at FOREX.com and FXEmpire are watching $3,500 per ounce as the next critical support floor, while Morgan Stanley (MS) named gold its top commodity pick for 2027.

data.title: 3 Vanguard ETFs Paying High Yields for Monthly Passive Income
data.description:
As stocks continue to lose ground and tech shares bear much of the selling, earning money without having to rely on market rallies is becoming appealing. For investors looking to put their money to work while navigating Wall Street's latest downturn, high-yield ETFs offer an attractive possibility: regular cash distributions, diversification, and the potential to build a steady stream of passive income.

Vanguard, one of the world's largest investment managers, offers several ETFs designed to deliver attractive income through monthly distributions. Using the TipRanks Best Vanguard ETFs tool, we've pinpointed three worth considering: Vanguard High-Yield Active ETF (VGHY), Vanguard Emerging Markets Government Bond ETF (VWOB), and Vanguard Long-Term Corporate Bond ETF (VCLT). Together, they offer yields exceeding 6%, monthly income potential, and exposure to three distinct segments of the bond market.

Vanguard High-Yield Active ETF (VGHY)

The Vanguard High-Yield Active ETF (VGHY) takes a relatively simple approach to generating income. It lends money to companies willing to pay higher interest rates, then passes much of that income along to investors. The catch is that these aren't necessarily Wall Street's safest borrowers. VGHY focuses on high-yield corporate bonds, commonly known as junk bonds, where greater credit risk comes with the potential for bigger payouts. And rather than following an index, Vanguard's portfolio managers actively decide which bonds are worth owning and which risks aren't worth taking.

VGHY charges an annual expense ratio of just 0.22%, while offering a 6.28% dividend yield. Better yet for income seekers, distributions arrive monthly rather than quarterly. As of October 31, the fund held 605 securities and managed about $312.7 million in assets. Among its largest recently disclosed positions were bonds associated with TransDigm and Nissan Motor Acceptance, alongside U.S. Treasury securities. No single position accounted for even 1% of the portfolio, meaning the fund isn't betting too heavily on any one borrower.

So, why might VGHY deserve a place in an income-focused portfolio? Consider someone investing $20,000. At a 6.28% annual yield, that translates into about $1,256 a year, or $105 per month, before taxes and assuming distributions remain unchanged. That's money arriving without having to sell shares or wait for the stock market to recover. Of course, higher yields aren't free money, and weaker borrowers can run into trouble when economic conditions deteriorate. Still, for investors comfortable taking on additional credit risk, VGHY offers a relatively inexpensive way to turn a diversified bond portfolio into a monthly income stream.

Vanguard Emerging Markets Government Bond ETF (VWOB)

The Vanguard Emerging Markets Government Bond ETF (VWOB) takes investors well beyond the U.S. bond market, putting their money to work in countries such as Argentina, Mexico, Brazil, and Saudi Arabia. Rather than lending primarily to companies, as VGHY does, this fund focuses on U.S. dollar-denominated bonds issued by emerging-market governments, government agencies, and state-owned enterprises. It's a way to collect interest from borrowers around the world without having to buy foreign bonds individually. And unlike VGHY, which relies on active portfolio managers, VWOB follows the Bloomberg USD Emerging Markets Government RIC Capped Index.

VWOB also comes with an attractive price tag, charging an annual expense ratio of just 0.15%, compared with VGHY's 0.22%. The fund offers a 6.20% dividend yield, with distributions paid monthly. Its portfolio contains more than 900 bond holdings, backed by ~$6.6 billion in total assets. Among its five largest individual positions are three Argentine government bonds and two bonds issued by Mexico's state-owned oil company, Pemex.

Of course, lending money to emerging-market governments comes with risks, including political instability, sovereign defaults, and changing interest rates. But for investors willing to accept those uncertainties, VWOB offers an inexpensive way to earn monthly income from countries that might otherwise be difficult to access.

Vanguard Long-Term Corporate Bond ETF (VCLT)

The Vanguard Long-Term Corporate Bond ETF (VCLT) takes another route to generating income, focusing on established companies rather than riskier corporate borrowers or emerging-market governments. The fund tracks the Bloomberg U.S. 10+ Year Corporate Bond Index, investing in investment-grade corporate bonds with maturities exceeding 10 years. That means investors are lending money to some of the biggest names in corporate America for extended periods, collecting interest along the way. The trade-off is that longer-term bonds are particularly sensitive to interest rate movements, meaning their market values can fall considerably when borrowing costs rise.

VCLT also happens to be the cheapest of the three Vanguard ETFs, charging an annual expense ratio of just 0.03%. The fund is also considerably larger, managing about $9.5 billion across 2,647 holdings. Among its largest corporate bond positions are Anheuser-Busch, CVS Health, Boeing, Meta Platforms, and Pfizer. Meanwhile, investors receive monthly distributions backed by an attractive 6.00% dividend yield.

For investors who can tolerate the volatility that comes with long-duration bonds, VCLT offers a low-cost way to collect monthly income from established corporate borrowers.

data.title: Microsoft Stock (NASDAQ:MSFT) Slips Despite New Team-Up Effort with Danaher
data.description:
Tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) recently got together with Danaher (DHR) to put together a line of instruments powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that carry out a variety of scientific tasks. The deal also calls for an "interoperable platform" to be built to help manage these tools effectively. Microsoft stock dropped nearly 2% in Friday afternoon's trading. Microsoft has posted a 4.15% rally in its share price over the past year.

The Team-Up Project

Danaher is a healthcare company, so when Microsoft got together with it, an opportunity arose to bring artificial intelligence into a field that can use it on several fronts. In fact, as Danaher described it, the two were building a common foundation that allowed both instruments and laboratories to work together consistently as one "connected Danaher."

Microsoft will bring both its Azure and Foundry tools to create a secure cloud infrastructure that is compliant with any applicable regulatory measures. Further, AI agents will also be set up that can handle instrument control as well as measure and interpret results generated from the instruments themselves. The partnership is expected to bear fruit before the end of the year as commercial applications start rolling out. This includes a new tool known as MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant for high-content cellular imaging systems.

Clear Your Schedule Now

If you could put down your copy of Grand Theft Auto 6 for a minute, you might be surprised to discover that Microsoft's Xbox division has a lot more waiting for you. This year's Black Friday 2026 sale has been announced, and the event will feature over 2,000 titles getting markdowns to one degree or another.

Some titles are clearly aimed at doorbuster status, like Dead Space, which will be selling for 90% off normal prices, and Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade, which will be selling for 85% off. Some titles will have much shallower discounts, but still be available for decent prices. For instance, Baldur's Gate 3 Deluxe Edition will be selling for 30% off, while Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced will be selling for 25% off. Regardless of your particular tastes, you will likely find something of interest if you own an Xbox.

Is Microsoft a Buy, Hold or Sell?

data.description:

Consumer Demand Remains Strong

Consumer demand has remained strong this year despite persistently high inflation. According to the latest U.S. Census Bureau Monthly Retail Trade Report, U.S. retail sales totaled $748.2 billion in October of this year, a 6.8% year-over-yearincrease.

data.title: Japanese Yen Leads G10 Currencies as Stock Sell-Off Threatens Carry Trades and Dollar Eyes Fourth Weekly Gain
data.description:
The Japanese yen (USD/JPY) jumped to the top of G10 currency rankings on Friday as a seven-day global stock sell-off drove investors toward safe havens. This also pulled the U.S. dollar down 0.60% against the yen to 158.75, TipRanks data shows.

Even with Friday's afternoon profit-taking, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) held near 103.8 and stayed on track for a fourth straight weekly gain.

Traders rushed out of riskier bets after Thursday's 1,101-point Dow plunge spilled into Asian and European chip shares. New inflation numbers out of Tokyo and emergency-stockpiling retail figures from London added large swings across major currency pairs ahead of December central bank meetings.

Japanese Yen (USD/JPY) Fights Back Near 160

After testing resistance near 160 earlier this week, USD/JPY reversed lower on Friday as rising stock market swings threatened yen carry trades, StoneX analysts noted. In a carry trade, investors borrow cheap yen to buy higher-yielding assets abroad, then rush to buy yen back when stocks tumble.

Hotter Japanese price data added fuel to the yen's rebound as core consumer inflation ticked up to 2.2% in October. This reading marked its fastest pace in 2026 after household utility subsidies expired.

This reading strengthened expectations for the Bank of Japan to raise its benchmark interest rate to 1.50% next month, with 61 of 71 economists in a Reuters poll backing a December hike.

U.S. Dollar (DXY) Rides December Fed Rate Hike Bets

Broader dollar demand has stayed firm all week as U.S. 10-year Treasury yields hovered near 5.02% and futures markets priced in a near-certain Federal Reserve rate increase on December 9, CME FedWatch data shows. Fed Governor Christopher Waller amplified that move on Wednesday when he called for a larger half-point hike to cool stubborn prices.

"We have to be a little more aggressive with our rate hikes to try to reduce inflation," Waller told CNBC. Traders also watched Friday remarks from Waller and Fed Governor Lisa Cook, who dissented in October in favor of an immediate hike, while J.P. Morgan (JPM) scrapped its single-hike call to forecast three straight Fed increases.

British Pound (GBP/USD) and Euro (EUR/USD) Cling to Lows

Overseas currencies found minor relief Friday afternoon after sliding to multi-month lows on Thursday, when foreign investors converted billions into dollars for Anthropic's (ANT) record Nasdaq (NDAQ) debut.

The British pound (GBP/USD) edged up 0.12% to $1.3103 after British retail sales unexpectedly rose 0.7% in October. Shoppers bought extra canned goods and long-life milk following a U.K. government emergency-preparedness campaign, Bloomberg noted.

Meanwhile, the euro (EUR/USD) ticked up 0.12% to $1.0981 after rebounding from a 19-month low of $1.0953 earlier this week. Still, a 1.7-percentage-point yield gap favoring U.S. two-year bonds over German debt continues to cap euro recoveries heading into next week's U.S. PCE inflation report.

data.title: SpaceX (SPX) vs. Anthropic (ANT): One Stock Is Worth Buying, the Other Is Too Risky, Says Investor
data.description:
The year 2026 will be remembered for the biggest IPOs in Wall Street history, with SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) making their blockbuster debuts just five months apart. SpaceX brought investors a chance to own a piece of Elon Musk's sprawling empire, spanning rockets, Starlink satellite internet, and an expanding AI infrastructure operation. Anthropic, meanwhile, opened the door to Claude, an AI powerhouse competing to become an essential technology for businesses worldwide.

But saying Anthropic picked the wrong time to go public might be an understatement. Wall Street was already struggling with concerns over whether the trillions being poured into AI infrastructure would ever generate sufficient returns. The Democrats' election victory added to those worries, raising fears of tougher AI regulation and restrictions on data center construction, while the scandal surrounding the godfather of AI, Jensen Huang, dealt another blow to confidence in the sector.

And Anthropic's arrival has done little to calm those nerves. The stock is falling about 10% during its first full trading session on Friday, weighing on tech shares across the market. SpaceX hasn't escaped the selling either, tumbling around 7% today and leaving its shares about 25% below its October high.

With both stocks taking a beating, investors may be wondering which of these two blockbuster IPOs offers the better buying opportunity. Investor Ricardo Fernandez has taken a close look at both and sees a clear winner. While he's bullish on one, he believes the other is simply too risky to buy right now.

Starting with SpaceX, Fernandez's concerns aren't about its technology or the talent behind it. Rather, the investor believes the company's expensive expansion into AI infrastructure raises serious doubts about whether investors will see adequate returns.

Fernandez is particularly skeptical of Musk's vision for orbital data centers, which would use SpaceX rockets to deploy computing infrastructure beyond Earth. Although the concept could eliminate certain electricity and land-related expenses, the investor argues that the costs of launching, maintaining, and eventually replacing equipment make the idea financially unattractive.

"The economics and physics don't add up," Fernandez warns.

According to Fernandez, the problem is that space-based data centers wouldn't last very long, meaning SpaceX would have to replace expensive equipment every few years. And with the company now shifting more of its computing plans back to Earth, the original vision is already looking less realistic.

And that brings Fernandez to another concern: financing. Unlike established tech giants such as Alphabet, SpaceX lacks a comparable stream of earnings from mature operations to support its enormous infrastructure investments. The investor estimates that the company's expansion could require more than $1 trillion in capital expenditures, potentially forcing it to borrow heavily or issue additional shares.

Fernandez also doubts whether Starlink's subscriber growth can deliver the cash needed to support these plans. Although he sees considerable potential in satellite communications and rocket services, those operations may not be enough to carry the financial burden.

That leaves Fernandez hesitant to recommend buying SpaceX shares, despite acknowledging the company's engineering capabilities and commercial opportunities.

"SPCX is a wait-and-see stock based on an aggressive data center expansion plan that has moved to Earth and will eventually rely on its own GPUs," the investor summed up, assigning SPCX a Hold (i.e., Neutral) rating.

Anthropic, however, tells a much more encouraging story in Fernandez's view. While the company's debut has been overshadowed by the technology sell-off, the investor believes its underlying financial performance offers evidence that customers are willing to pay serious money for AI services.

According to Fernandez's projections, Anthropic's annual revenue could reach about $55 billion in 2026, with enterprise customers contributing around $44 billion. Consumer and professional subscriptions would account for another $11 billion, demonstrating that Claude's appeal extends well beyond developers experimenting with new technology.

The company's approach to infrastructure is another advantage. Rather than relying entirely on computing facilities it builds itself, Anthropic combines capacity from providers such as Amazon and Google with investments in dedicated infrastructure. This approach allows it to expand computing resources while concentrating on developing models, improving its products, and growing customer relationships.

Fernandez estimates that Anthropic could generate around $10 billion in adjusted operating income this year, with profitability improving as revenue expands and research expenses become a smaller proportion of sales.

The investor also believes the company's growing presence in enterprise software could help it become more valuable to customers, particularly as Claude Code and other offerings become integrated into everyday professional tasks.

His confidence comes through clearly in his conclusion: "I rate ANT a Buy: ANT is the litmus test for AI monetization."

Wall Street, however, doesn't seem to think investors need to choose between the two. SpaceX holds a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 28 Buys, 6 Holds, and one Sell. Its average price target of $263.83 suggests a 105% upside over the next 12 months. Anthropic also enjoys a Strong Buy consensus, with 6 Buys and one Hold. Its average target of $133.33 points to a potential gain of 57% from current levels. (See SPCX stock forecast or ANT stock forecast)
